messages:
Alex R: Heads up - ACME support ticket says p99 for /v1/generate jumped from ~600ms to ~3.8s around 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC right after the canary deploy. Error rate unchanged. They attached trace ids trc-abc123 / trc-def456. Tagging @Nadia (oncall) to triage.

Nadia (oncall): On it. Pulling traces and live metrics. Any quick repro steps from support?

Alex R: They repro with their normal traffic pattern (batch size ~1, seq len 512). Occurs mostly eu-west-1. Model listed in ticket: redwood/gpt-3.8-xxq-quant (canary).

Devin P: Looking at cluster events now. Noting autoscaler evictions at 01:58 UTC and a spike in host CPU for the canary slice -> possible CPU fallback to slower execution path.

Maya S: If it's CPU fallback + batching mismatch we can: 1) rollback canary 2) divert eu-west traffic to v1.11.3 3) enable smaller model fallback for ACME until root cause. 

OpsBot: Deploy: canary v1.11.4 -> started 2026-03-15T01:52:11Z on pool canary-eu-west. Health checks passed at 01:55Z.

Nadia (oncall): Quick mitigation checklist I'm going to run (will call each step when done):
- STEP A: Pause canary -> command: `infra deploy pause --canary canary-eu-west`
- STEP B: Re-route ACME endpoint to stable model -> `routes set acme /v1/generate --model redwood/gpt-3.8-xxq-stable --region eu-west-1`
- STEP C: Apply per-customer emergency rate limit 10rps -> `rls apply --customer acme --limit 10 --window 1s`
- STEP D: Enable circuit-breaker policy for p99>1.5s -> console: Policies > CB > new: p99>1500ms, actions=[throttle, fallback]

Nadia (oncall): Doing STEP A now.

OpsBot: Canary canary-eu-west paused (initiated by Nadia).

Nadia (oncall): STEP B applied. ACME route now pinned to redwood/gpt-3.8-xxq-stable.

Alex R: :thumbsup: support confirmed initial requests improve after routing change, p99 dropping toward ~800ms on their sample stream.

Maya S: I'm going to enable model variant fallback for that endpoint: smaller quantized variant redwood/gpt-3.8-mini-qq that has predictable p99 under load. CLI: `routes fallback add acme /v1/generate --model redwood/gpt-3.8-mini-qq --trigger p99>1200ms --grace 60s`

Devin P: Investigating root cause: kernel selection on canary hosts changed (new cudnn minor). Looks like scheduler now picks different attention kernel for long sequences causing slower per-token time when the KV cache hot path isn't used. Rolling back kernel patch on canary seems safest.

Nadia (oncall): STEP C rate limit applied. STEP D circuit breaker policy created. Monitoring p99 for 10m.

support-bot: Ticket #ACME-482 updated: we applied routing fallback and rate limits, customer notified.

Alex R: Customer says latency stabilized for the last ~3 minutes but would like root cause. Thanks team.

Maya S: Follow-up remediation plan (succinct):
1) Roll back kernel patch on canary hosts and repro load test in staging.
2) Add automated guardrail: if canary p99 increases >1.2x baseline within 15m, auto-pause canary and route traffic to stable. (Implement as: `alerts create --metric p99 --window 15m --threshold 1.2 --action pause-canary,notify`)
3) Expand CB policy templates: per-customer rate limits + model fallback pre-configs for EU regions.
4) Postmortem and add a lightweight synthetic test exercising long-seq KV cache hot path in PR gate.

Devin P: I'll open a CL to pin kernel versions for canary until we validate performance.

Nadia (oncall): Leaving monitoring for 30m. If p99 creeps again, execute full rollback and escalate to infra. For now customer escalation closed by support with notes.

Alex R: Great work. Please add runbook snippet to eng-oncall playbooks: quick actions for customer-facing p99 regressions (pause canary, pin route, limit rps, CB fallback, notify customer).

Maya S: Will add PR to playbooks repo and link incident ids.

Nadia (oncall): Closing thread if no further regressions in 30m. Thanks all.

Devin P: FYI I'll include perf graphs and kernel diffs in the follow-up ticket.
